complexity.notes: The chained elif with short-circuit `stack.pop()` calls is correct (pop only executes when the bracket type matches the condition) but hard to read; a dict mapping closing to opening brackets, or comparing against stack.pop() once, would be cleaner. Also `bracket in "({["` (string membership) is more idiomatic than a list literal. Correctness does not depend on hashing.
complexity.summary: Classic stack-based validation: push each opening bracket, and on each closing bracket pop and verify the matching type, returning False on any mismatch or empty stack. At the end, the string is valid iff the stack is empty.
